beats.text: Your team spends hours every week matching delivery paperwork to shipments by hand.
Here's what that looks like when an agent does the grunt work — and a person stays in charge.
Quick note before we start: this is a concept build, not a client project.
Every name, shipment, and document you're about to see is fictional.
The problem is real, though.
Shipping documents land in different inboxes and folders.
Someone has to match each one to its shipment, spot what's missing, and chase it down.
That's the work this agent takes on.
Fifty shipment records, forty documents.

beats.label: 3,215 vs 2,715 lb
beats.say: Here's shipment eight: the paperwork says three thousand two hundred fifteen pounds, the record says two thousand seven hundred fifteen.
beats.text: Here's shipment eight: the paperwork says 3,215 pounds, the record says 2,715.
The agent puts both numbers side by side so a reviewer sees the mismatch instantly — with a link back to the original PDF.

beats.label: No matching shipment
beats.text: And when a reference doesn't match anything? It goes to a human for review.

beats.label: No matching shipment
beats.text: Nothing gets guessed.
The agent drafts the follow-up email naming the issue.
A person reviews the evidence and hits approve or reject.

beats.label: Nothing sent yet
beats.text: Notice: approving doesn't send anything.

beats.label: Separate send action
beats.text: That's a separate action, enforced by the system — not just the button.
Rejected drafts can't be sent, and if the evidence changes, old approvals expire.
The reviewer sends it to a demo outbox — a local simulation.

beats.label: .invalid domain
beats.text: No real email ever leaves; every recipient is on a non-deliverable domain.
Safe to demo, but the real approval and send logic is running underneath.
The outbox keeps the approved message so anyone can inspect exactly what went out.
The agent reads source records without changing them, only touches files in the current job, and logs every action.
On the test fixtures: all 30 clean documents matched.
beats.say: On the test fixtures: all thirty clean documents matched.

beats.text: All 11 planted issues and 65 missing-document gaps caught.
beats.say: All eleven planted issues and sixty-five missing-document gaps caught.

beats.text: Zero false positives.
Those are deterministic results on fictional data — not a promise about your operation.
But they show the shape of what's possible.
If paperwork is eating your team's week, the next step is a two-week audit of one workflow.
